text:
leila: Heads-up — MedLink POC hit a stream chop during chart-summary generation. UI shows "Unexpected end of JSON input" and the app logs `req=mx-77b`. Happened around 90s in the demo. Can we triage?
sam: Oof. Is the client desktop/mobile? Which SDK and model?
leila: Electron-based kiosk using desktop-sdk v1.1.3. Model: gpt-4o-stream-v1 (hosted). Customer gateway sits behind a corporate proxy (they said F5+some gateway appliance).
carlos: Ask them for raw headers and whether the proxy adds Content-Encoding or Content-Length. Common anti-pattern: proxy computes content-length (buffers) or injects gzip which breaks streaming.
leila: They sent headers: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Encoding: gzip`, and `Content-Length: 0`. Also saw `X-Proxy-Buffered: true` from their appliance logs.
sam: That combination is classic buffering. If proxy tries to gzip then buffer to compute content-length it will close/trim the connection mid-stream. Two fixes: (1) customer: disable buffering/compression for SSE endpoints (whitelist path), (2) us: enable periodic SSE comments/heartbeats and reduce our flush size for this tenant.
carlos: For the client: ensure SSE parser accumulates data until the blank line delimiter; do not attempt to parse per chunk. Also handle partial utf-8 by concatenating bytes and decoding only on complete sequences.
leila: I'm sending them an F5 config snippet and a small checklist. Sam — can you flip a tenant flag to flush more frequently for the demo?
sam: Yes — toggled tenant debug flush to 128 bytes. Also created assist ticket POC-5022. infra-bot: ticket created: POC-5022 assigned to sam and carlos. Link: https://redwood.support/tickets/POC-5022
leila: They applied the whitelist and disabled response buffering. Re-test scheduled for 11:30 PT. Will report back. Thanks! :pray:
